summary: iter184 — P0 regression confirmed FIXED. Re-tested GET /api/payments/status/{session_id} after main agent's fix (added `_db = get_db()` inside try-block, made auth Optional, added PII gate via _auth(credentials)). 12/12 backend tests pass: 5 HTTP smoke tests (no NameError crash on bad/invalid/anon/bad-token sessions; both Admin + Buyer credentials login OK) + 7 function-level tests with mocked Stripe + seeded payment_transactions row covering the full PII matrix (anon, buyer, seller, admin, stranger) plus two no-crash edge cases (missing txn row, missing seller user). The `db is not defined` NameError that silently swallowed seller_contact in iter183 is gone.

minor.issue: Stripe error path returns the full stripe.StripeError message in HTTPException detail (e.g., 'Invalid checkout.session id: cs_invalid_xyz_123'). This is acceptable for now but leaks Stripe-internal error wording to anonymous callers. Consider returning a generic 'Invalid session' for unauthenticated requests.

action_items: None — P0 fully resolved. The iter183 P2 'add auth on /payments/status' concern is now ALSO addressed (Optional Bearer + PII gate via _auth + buyer/seller/admin role check). Frontend PaymentSuccessPage already sends Bearer token when available, so the buyer flow will see seller_contact end-to-end.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/routes/payments.py get_checkout_status: NameError fix is correct; the bare `except Exception: pass` from iter183 has also been replaced with `except Exception as e: logger.warning(...)` — perfect. Future regressions of this kind will surface in logs.
/app/backend/routes/payments.py: _auth() helper is well-designed (returns None on failure for optional auth, raises for required-auth callers via FastAPI). Same wrapper used everywhere — DRY.

Consider: the fixture function _mock_paid_session in our test file could be moved into a shared conftest.py if more payment-status tests are added in future iterations (so other testers don't re-implement).

seed_data_creation: Per-test seed: TEST_-prefixed payment_transactions + users docs created and torn down inside async fixtures. No persistent test data left behind.
context_for_next_testing_agent: P0 bug from iter183 is fully fixed and verified. The function now: (1) initialises _db = get_db() inside the try-block, (2) accepts Optional Bearer credentials, (3) gates seller_contact behind a buyer/seller/admin PII check, (4) logs (instead of swallowing) enrichment failures. End-to-end Stripe verification was not possible because no paid sessions exist in the live Stripe account — function-level tests with mocked stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve cover the contract instead. To verify against a real paid session, complete a Stripe checkout for any active listing then GET /api/payments/status/{cs_xxx} as the buyer (with Authorization Bearer token).
rca_of_the_issue: Verified fix matches iter183's recommended one-liner: `_db = get_db()` is now the first statement inside the try-block at routes/payments.py:225. Additionally, the bare `except Exception: pass` was upgraded to `except Exception as e: logger.warning(...)` so future regressions of this kind are observable. The function's contract is now: anonymous → status fields only (no PII); buyer/seller/admin → status + listing_id + seller_contact; everyone else → status + listing_id (no PII). All 12 tests confirm this contract.
